# COMMON HOURS

## Identity
- Project: COMMON HOURS
- Entrance phrase: Time together, room to pause
- Building use: intergenerational community station
- Users: children, caregivers, older residents and station staff
- Direction: retained single-storey brick station with an eastern single-storey extension

## Site and levels

- Axes: x east; y north; all plan coordinates in mm
- Site: 28000 × 20000 mm
- Existing footprint: x 4000–16000; y 4000–12000
- Existing external dimensions: 12000 × 8000 mm
- Extension envelope: x 16000–25000; y 4000–16000
- Extension envelope dimensions: 9000 × 12000 mm
- Existing and new finished floor: ±0.000
- Forecourt level: ±0.000
- Existing clear height: 3000 mm
- Existing roof soffit: +3.000 m
- Existing roof top: +3.400 m
- New room clear height: 3200 mm
- New roof height limit: +4.200 m
- Southern site setback: 4000 mm
- Eastern extension setback: 3000 mm

## Retention and materials

- Existing door openings: D-01 and D-02, each 2000 mm wide
- Extension connection: D-02 in W-04
- Existing external walls: 200 mm buff brick, exposed finish
- Existing corner columns: reinforced concrete, 200 × 200 mm
- Existing roof: reinforced concrete, 400 mm overall depth
- New structure: independent glulam posts and beams, exposed internally
- New external cladding: timber rainscreen
- New window frames: aluminium

## Use and operation
- Shared Room capacity: 20 people

- Quiet access route: at least 1500 mm clear, from Connecting Lobby

- Phase 1: weekday extension construction with existing services operating
- Phase 2: Sunday connection at D-02, 09:00–17:00

steps.userMessage:
COMMON HOURS | An extension for a working intergenerational community station

Our community station brings children, caregivers and older residents together six days a week. We need a single-storey extension with a Shared Room for 20 people, a Quiet Room for 8 people, a Connecting Lobby and an Activity Store. Give the Quiet Room a view into shared activity and a separate approach: its access route must remain clear when tables, games and group sessions occupy the Shared Room. Print "COMMON HOURS" and "Time together, room to pause" at the completed public entrance.

The site measures 28000 × 20000 mm. The existing brick building measures 12000 × 8000 mm; its floor is ±0.000, roof soffit +3.000 m and roof top +3.400 m. The eastern extension envelope measures 9000 × 12000 mm, with a maximum roof height of +4.200 m. Retain columns C-01 and C-02, walls W-01 to W-04, roof R-01 and the two existing door openings. The new connection uses the 2000 mm opening D-02 in W-04. Existing services operate Monday–Saturday, 09:00–18:00; the building and southern forecourt remain available throughout those hours. Connection work occupies Sunday, 09:00–17:00, with services resuming Monday at 09:00. Keep existing buff brick exposed; use exposed glulam posts and beams inside the extension, timber rainscreen outside and aluminium window frames. The retained building and these material decisions establish the direction.

Audience: children, caregivers, older residents and station staff, together with the community operator, for agreement on the extension layout and the sequence that keeps daily services running.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the project identity, building limits and operating commitments. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-site-and-retention.en.md records coordinates, openings and retained components. 04-rooms-and-operations.en.md records room areas, capacities, adjacencies and service hours. existing-site-survey.png provides the measured plan, section and protected operating areas. existing-station-front.png establishes the existing entrance, brickwork and street elevation. everyday-forecourt.png provides atmosphere from children, caregivers and older residents using the existing forecourt.

Deliverables:
1. A two-page programme specification with all eight room IDs, names, net areas, clear heights, capacities, adjacencies and floor levels, plus the retained-component list and operating hours
2. One existing-building survey and retention sheet with the site boundary, four walls, two columns, roof, openings and component IDs
3. One completed site plan with the existing footprint, extension envelope, proposed footprint, public entrance and eastern construction access
4. One dimensioned ground-floor plan with all eight rooms, their IDs and net areas, retained-component IDs and the new connection through D-02
5. One section through the existing Service Hall, D-02 and extension, with floor levels, clear heights, roof levels and existing and new construction identified
6. One elevation sheet with south and east elevations, opening dimensions and material boundaries
7. One junction detail through the new roof and W-04, with the independent glulam support, exposed brick, weather seal and roof drainage
8. Two construction and operation sheets: Phase 1 for weekday extension construction beside the operating station, and Phase 2 for the Sunday connection and Monday reopening
9. One completed-occupation plan with 20 Shared Room places, 8 Quiet Room places, intergenerational sightlines and a separate quiet access route at least 1500 mm clear
10. Two eye-level perspectives: the completed public entrance and an interior view showing the Shared Room, Quiet Room and their connecting circulation
11. One 10-second video moving from the retained entrance through the connection into the completed extension
12. One presentation document of at least 10 pages, reusing the specification, survey, plans, section, elevations, junction, phase sheets and perspectives

Acceptance:
- The programme specification, ground-floor plan and presentation repeat E-01 Service Hall 57 m², E-02 Staff Room 9.6 m², E-03 Toilets 11.6 m², E-04 Store 8.4 m², N-01 Shared Room 48 m², N-02 Quiet Room 18 m², N-03 Connecting Lobby 12 m² and N-04 Activity Store 6 m². The specification and section state 3000 mm existing clear height, 3200 mm new clear height and the shared floor datum ±0.000.
- The survey, site plan and ground-floor plan carry a north arrow and metric scale bar. The survey, ground-floor plan, phase sheets and presentation retain C-01, C-02, W-01 to W-04 and D-01/D-02 at the recorded coordinates; the survey, section and junction detail retain R-01 at +3.000 m soffit and +3.400 m roof top. The site plan and section place the extension inside its 9000 × 12000 mm envelope and below +4.200 m.
- The two construction and operation sheets label Monday–Saturday 09:00–18:00 service access through D-01, the protected existing building and southern forecourt, and worker access from the east gate. Phase 2 also labels Sunday 09:00–17:00 connection work at D-02 and Monday 09:00 reopening; the presentation repeats this sequence.
- The ground-floor and completed-occupation plans give N-02 a route at least 1500 mm clear from N-03, with activity circulation routed outside it. The occupation plan shows 20 places in N-01, 8 in N-02 and a sightline between the rooms; the interior perspective uses the same partition and opening arrangement.
- The section, elevations and junction detail identify exposed existing buff brick, exposed internal glulam posts and beams, timber rainscreen and aluminium window frames in their applicable locations. The two perspectives and video match the plans and elevations in single-storey massing, roof profiles, opening positions and material boundaries.
- The entrance perspective and video opening frame display "COMMON HOURS" and "Time together, room to pause" at the public entrance. The presentation repeats both strings on its first page and reuses the earlier work across at least 10 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
